messages:
Alicia: FYI we just got an escalation from a Dedicated customer — they report a jump in tail latency after applying a new quantization profile to their pool. p95 and p99 both spiked.
Alicia: Customer summary: before profile change p95 ~110ms / p99 ~210ms. After applying qprof-2026-03-int8fp8 p95 ~320ms / p99 ~820ms. No errors returned by API, throughput steady.
Kevin: Do we have model id and exact profile name they used? Need to map to our rollout artifacts.
Alicia: model_id: open-lorax-3b-v2, quant_profile: qprof-2026-03-int8fp8. They flipped it on their Dedicated pool ~02:14 UTC last night via Console.
Marta: tagging eng-ml — any known fp8 calibration oddities with that profile? Could be calibration re-runs or per-request fallbacks.
Ben: Infra snapshot: GPU utilization stable, but CPU time increased on the runtime node serving their pool during the spike window. Also noticed more context-switches per second.
Kevin: Increased CPU on runtime node usually points to extra software work — maybe per-request dequant/quant checks or fallback handling. Alicia, can you request an anonymized repro payload and the invocation settings (batch size, max_tokens, prompt length, caching)?
Alicia: Repro details received: synchronous generate, batch_size=1, max_tokens=512, prompt ~400 tokens => total sequence ~900. They have client-side prefix KV cache enabled.
Marta: That sequence length explains part of it. Our int8 kernels for long sequences sometimes switch to hybrid kernels that have higher per-token latency. And fp8 calibration can trigger expensive checks during warmup.
Kevin: Runtime logs around the rollout window — look for "quant-calib" or "fallback-to-fp16" strings.
Alicia: Snippets from their runtime logs (timestamps preserved):
```
[2026-03-12T02:14:05Z] INFO quantizer: applying profile qprof-2026-03-int8fp8 to open-lorax-3b-v2
[2026-03-12T02:14:05Z] WARN quantizer: calibration mismatch for layer attn.wq -> running slow re-calibration
[2026-03-12T02:14:05Z] INFO runtime: kernel_select -> hybrid_kern_v2 for seq_len>512
[2026-03-12T02:14:06Z] INFO runtime: fallback_policy -> executing fp16 path for 1.2% requests
```
Alicia: They also show repeated calibration log entries during the warmup period.
Marta: OK that matches my hypothesis: re-calibration on deploy + hybrid kernels for seq_len>512 + occasional fp16 fallback produce latency outliers and extra CPU work. The calibration step is expensive and if it runs more than once per node it will affect p99.
Kevin: Short-term mitigation options:
- Route the customer to the fp16 model variant (open-lorax-3b-v2:fp16)
- Roll them back to the earlier, conservative quant profile (qprof-2026-02-int8-safe)
- Disable prefix KV caching temporarily on the client to reduce interactions
- Pin them to a pre-warmed node
Alicia: Customer asked for a quick toggle. What's the minimal API call we can give them to force the fp16 variant on Dedicated?
Kevin: Use admin route override for Dedicated customers, example:
```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/admin/route/override \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN_TOKEN" \
  -d '{"customer_id":"acct-123","route":{"model":"open-lorax-3b-v2:fp16","policy":"force"}}'
```
Kevin: Or Console -> Dedicated -> Pool -> Model overrides -> pick the fp16 variant and force.
Ben: Infra can also provision a canary node with pre-warmed hybrid kernels and replay their payloads to validate.
Marta: For root cause we need to reproduce with a seq_len~900 workload and the qprof-2026-03-int8fp8 tarball. My plan:
1) Reproduce p50/p95/p99 with batch_size=1 across qprof-2026-02-int8-safe, qprof-2026-03-int8fp8, and fp16.
2) Instrument calibration path to see if calibration occurs once at load or is retriggering per request.
3) Add counters to traces for calibration runs and fallback-to-fp16 events.
Ben: I'll pull the artifacts and spin up a canary cluster. Need S3 path for the profile/checkpoint.
Alicia: Artifacts uploaded to s3://redwood-repro/open-lorax/3b/qprof-2026-03-int8fp8.tar.gz. Filed ticket INC-2345 (incident-bot linked it).
incident-bot: Created ticket INC-2345: "Dedicated: p95/p99 regression after quant profile qprof-2026-03-int8fp8" assigned to eng-ml.
Kevin: Immediate recommended steps for support to tell the customer:
- Switch to the fp16 variant (we applied this for one customer and saw p95 drop to ~130ms, p99 ~260ms)
- If they need quantized inference, revert to qprof-2026-02-int8-safe until we validate qprof-2026-03
- Pause automatic quant_profile rollouts and require 0.1% canary traffic for Dedicated
- If acceptable, turn off prefix KV caching while we iterate
Alicia: We applied the fp16 override for them. They confirmed immediate improvement (p95 ~130ms). They're keeping the override while we investigate further.
Marta: Engineering action items:
- eng-ml: fix calibration logic so calibration runs on model load only; add unit/integration tests around long sequences
- eng-runtime: add a guard to avoid per-request calibration rechecks, emit metric runtime.quant.calib_rechecks
- eng-runtime: add a safer default rollout policy for quant profiles (strict canary + health checks)
- infra: provide prewarming scripts for hybrid kernels and document when they are needed for long-seq workloads
- support: KB update with rollback steps and a checklist for quant_profile canaries
Kevin: I'll prototype a runtime flag to mark a profile "calibrated" on a node for N minutes and skip heavy calibration checks while still validating numeric safety via sampling.
Marta: Also propose a model-level whitelist for enabling fp8 by default. Not all architectures respond well to fp8; we should surface a warning in Console when a user picks an fp8-capable profile for a model not on the whitelist.
Alicia: I'll keep the customer updated. Plan: monitor metrics 24h after override, then close the escalation and create a postmortem doc referencing INC-2345.
Ben: Repro run starting now on canary; will report perf numbers in the ticket.
Marta: I'll attach profiling traces and per-layer calibration costs to INC-2345 when done.
Kevin: Looping in Product for visibility (cc @Product). We might want a small UI change to highlight quantization risk and the rollback path in Dedicated pools.
Product: Thanks for the heads-up. We'll prioritize a Console notice and an in-UI rollback button for Dedicated.
Alicia: Closing the loop here for now; will post final metrics to the ticket. Thanks team. :thumbsup:
